preconditions.description: The number of servers n is an integer between 1 and 30,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(rules) == 4 * n and all(1 <= a <= n and 1 <= b <= n and 1 <= c <= n for (a, b, c) in rules)
preconditions.description: There are exactly 4n rules, each with server numbers a_i, b_i, c_i in the range 1 to n inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(rules.count((a, _, _)) == 4 for a in range(1, n + 1))
preconditions.description: Each server number from 1 to n appears exactly four times as a_i in the rules.

preconditions.expression: sum(1 for (_, b, _) in rules) + sum(1 for (_, _, c) in rules) == 8 * n
preconditions.description: The total number of b_i and c_i across all rules is exactly 8n.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= i <= 4 * n for i in range(1, 4 * n + 1))
preconditions.description: Rule indices are integers from 1 to 4n inclusive.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == 'NO' or (stdout.strip() == 'YES' and len(permutation) == 4 * n and set(permutation) == set(range(1, 4 * n + 1)))
postconditions.description: If no valid order exists, output is 'NO'. Otherwise, output is 'YES' followed by a permutation of rule indices 1 to 4n.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == 'YES' and all(1 <= process_count[server] <= 9 for server in range(1, n + 1) for process_count in simulate_rules(permutation, rules, n))
postconditions.description: The permutation of rules ensures that at every step, no server has more than 9 processes (old and new combined). The `simulate_rules` function tracks process counts per server after each rule application.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == 'YES' and all(process_count[server] == 8 for server in range(1, n + 1)) if (permutation := [int(x) for x in stdout.split()[1:]]) else True
postconditions.description: After applying all rules in the permutation, each server has exactly 8 processes.
